neighbours.label: 'what' as the object of a verb of discovery or observation (found, spotted, detected what ...), introducing something not yet identified, as against 'what' in embedded questions and discovery verbs with a plain object
fire: Divers off the coast have discovered what looks like a sunken ship.
The rover has detected what may be traces of ancient water.
Hikers in the park spotted what appeared to be a wolf.
Doctors noticed what seemed to be a small shadow on the scan.
The telescope has captured what researchers call a stellar nursery.
Farmers uncovered what turned out to be a Roman coin hoard.
Satellites have observed what look like huge dust storms.
Police found what they believe is the stolen car.
quiet: Divers off the coast asked what the old ship had carried.
The rover team wondered what the rocks were made of.
Hikers in the park spotted a wolf near the river.
Doctors explained what the small shadow on the scan meant.
The telescope has captured a stellar nursery in great detail.
Farmers uncovered a Roman coin hoard while plowing.
Satellites have observed huge dust storms on the planet.
Police told reporters what they knew about the stolen car.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.6 on ' what' after found/spotted/detected; 'asked/explained what' and plain objects below 0.1
notes: Card: 'demonstrated⟦ what⟧ they can do', 'has spotted⟦ what⟧ appear to be massive "baby" galaxies', 'things⟦ that⟧ never were', 'returning to⟦ what⟧ we knew'. Probe: 'have found what seem to be very young galaxies' 0.620, 'things that never were' 0.509; 'showed what their robot can do' 0.051, 'asked me what time it was' 0.003, 'What a beautiful day' 0.044, 'returned to what we had known' 0.141.
